after.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
after.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
claim_policy: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not make software free or open source, and final royalties, reference-code rights, certification fees and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.

Present Adam’s roughly ten-year price outlook as a strategic expectation, not an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

stage.label: Customer choice
stage.description: Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

stage.label: Applications across computers
stage.description: Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

stage.label: Business applications
stage.description: Demonstrate Abacus, then independent BPI records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that BPI has a Model II port.

stage.label: FlexiBUS peripherals
stage.description: Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

stage.label: Apple II and S-100 expansion products
stage.description: Present the Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II alongside the S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative joins the native Apple demonstration. Explain the drivers, optional display hardware and separate S-100 support without suggesting Apple endorses S-100 systems.

stage.label: Independent partners
stage.description: DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

stage.label: Preparing for the next generation
stage.description: Adam explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

stage.label: Availability and next steps
stage.description: Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_content.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

marketing_content.type: Apple II and S-100 product sheet
marketing_content.description: The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit.

Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence and royalty terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and fees, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

From his 1979 perspective, Adam does not expect a next-generation computer using an existing television and basic storage to fall below roughly USD 100 for about a decade. The figure is nominal US retail pricing before tax, excluding a new screen and a complete disk-and-printer business configuration; the exact basic-storage allowance is unresolved. The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television, so such a product requires separate engineering and costing.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent BPI branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 50 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
before.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral manufacturers to the published compatibility programmes, and help existing customers carry their applications and documents across supported systems.

steps.description: Begin confidential briefings and engineering-kit evaluations. Prioritise North Star and Vector Graphic as prospects; approach Cromemco, Altos, Intertec and Heath selectively. Invitations are not signed agreements or qualified products.

Alongside the existing DRI portable-extension release, publish separate CP/M application, FlexiBUS peripheral and optional Logix display compatibility profiles, reference-driver and test access, non-exclusive implementation principles and support-roadmap requirements. Exact fees and support duration remain to be settled.

Invite computer, software and peripheral suppliers to test named configurations and document failures before public demonstrations. Supplier attendance and passing results must be verified; no announcement of an unsigned OEM.

Present a 50-minute cross-vendor campaign before questions. Demonstrate applications/documents, then independent BPI, FlexiBUS, Apple native drivers and optional video. BPI management speaks with partners. State that the next generation breaks native Z80 binary compatibility; C source/API portability reduces migration work and a planned optional Z80 compatibility coprocessor supports qualified legacy software. Reveal neither processor word size nor architecture before NCC 1980. See ncc_1979_campaign.json.

Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Teach documented APIs, file interchange, C portability boundaries and device-class drivers. Publish a directory distinguishing shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.

Promote the separately recorded Tandy customer release and only individually qualified SMC or peripheral products. Update directory evidence; do not imply all licensed chips, every peripheral class or new independent OEM systems are shipping.

Target Tandy shipping, one additional named OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension/FlexiBUS option, another OEM in qualification, dealer/integrator configurations and third-party devices in several categories. These are adoption targets, not recorded achievements or contracted orders.

Publish verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Target three to five non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations by NCC 1980, counting Tandy once and excluding duplicate dealer builds. Do not disclose the new processor architecture early.
existing anchors / Tandy: Existing agreement: CP/M, native display adapter, FlexiBUS option and Abacus; no video requirement or BPI port.
existing anchors / Apple: Existing native expansion cooperation and peripheral/display demonstrations; no Z80 or CP/M execution provided.

after.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
after.description: Prepare the compatibility programme and partner demonstrations, deliver the NCC 1979 presentation and expansion-product launch, then run recruitment, dealer activity and qualification follow-up through the January 1980 review. Campaign.ncc1979 supplies the messages, presentation and marketing materials.

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch provides the working platform and business applications used to prepare cross-vendor demonstrations.
The Tandy cooperation agreement provides the basis for the Model II prototype and application-interchange work.
The limited Apple cooperation agreement provides documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II products.

Prepare named configurations, host-specific drivers, documented transfer paths and measured resource limits. Protect future architecture information and clear partner participation before public demonstrations.

outcomes.description: Published compatibility profiles, implementation guidance and records of unresolved access and support terms.
Rehearsed demonstration configurations, interoperability test records and an issue register distinguishing verified behaviour from limitations.
The NCC presentation and expansion-product launch have been delivered, with native Apple and S-100 support described separately and partner responsibilities retained.

An updated compatibility directory, recruitment and qualification records, dealer and developer materials, and an evidence-based closing review. Adoption and sales targets are not treated as achieved outcomes.

steps.description: Evaluate recruitment prospects and engineering kits. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration or distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Preserve existing applications and display investment; interest does not constitute an agreement.

Treat North Star and Vector as strong CP/M prospects with moderately strong FlexiBUS prospects; optional Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Cromemco is a moderate CP/M and FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its own OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited Logix-video potential; no platform redesign is assumed. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential, with limited Logix-video interest; plan late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification, not June availability. Heath/Heathkit has moderate CP/M and host-specific FlexiBUS potential but limited Logix-video interest; treat it as later feasibility work, not a promised 1979 release. These assessments guide outreach and do not establish commitments.
Publish compatibility profiles and provide reference-driver and test access alongside the separate DRI extension release. Record unresolved commercial and support terms.

Prepare the presentation space, audiovisual equipment and qualified demonstration systems. Test document round trips, disk formats, memory limits, loading, recalculation and device behaviour. Review all public material for the embargo and secure partner clearance.
Run supplier workshops, test named configurations and record failures and required corrections before public demonstrations.
Deliver the NCC presentation and the combined Apple II/S-100 expansion-product launch using the approved campaign materials and qualified systems.
Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Maintain a directory that distinguishes shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.
Update availability evidence for the separately recorded Tandy release and individually qualified SMC and peripheral products. Keep future products out of shipping claims.
Review progress against the campaign’s adoption targets using verified OEM configurations, qualifications and third-party device availability.

Track compatible-computer sell-through across vendors, qualified application editions, peripheral shipments and supported device classes, document-interchange results, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Count distinct manufacturers rather than duplicate dealer builds or SKUs.

Prepare the closing review with verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Report progress toward NCC 1980 goals without claiming unverified results or disclosing future architecture.

Continue the independent implementation and supplier approach established in the CP/M phase, covering documented software interfaces, compatible products and non-ERA port feasibility. DRI’s 68k effort remains development and validation work rather than a released port or licence income.

inputs.description: Supplier cooperation, documented interfaces and independent implementation practices established in the CP/M / 8-bit programme provide a foundation for the Artemis phase. CP/M ecosystem work continues alongside Artemis until April 1981; completion of the whole CP/M programme is not a prerequisite for Artemis work.
The completed AIONix development phase provides the operating-system foundation for Artemis-era integration and ecosystem work.

steps.description: Coordinate documented AIONix interfaces, developer access and compatible-product qualification while distinguishing supplier commitments, prototypes and released configurations.
Review selective native C/TUI application ports on 30 June 1980, testing files and arithmetic while retaining CP/M editions; source compatibility does not imply native execution of Z80 binaries.
Record independent vendors' interface-adapter qualification on 30 September 1980, including electrical and protocol conformance, supported configurations and optional AION certification.
Review 1980 sales, production capacity and investment on 31 December 1980, preserving the scenario's costed-production assumptions and 5% commercial capacity headroom.
Begin DRI’s independently licensed 68k AIONix port programme, including funded feasibility work, suitable external-MMU hardware assessment and restartable-fault investigation.

outcomes.description: The phase provides a framework for AIONix/Artemis ecosystem cooperation and records the start of DRI’s non-ERA port work. A completed 68k port, licence receipts and universal compatibility are not established by these activities.

before.title: Autodesk funded development and acceptance
before.description: Autodesk funded development and acceptance Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

inputs.description: The founders organising meeting on 30 January 1982 precedes the agreement that starts the funded development programme on 31 January. Attendees remain unspecified.
Native AIONix/ERA build with reliable floating-point geometry and typed coordinate entry
Dual-display driver with colour command/status screen and 800x600 drawing canvas; independent palettes and explicit input focus
Explicit CAD mouse integration; standard TUI mouse support alone is insufficient
Drawing load/save and DXF exchange tests against the other supported AutoCAD builds
Supported pen-plotter output and physical drawing verification
Measured RAM, storage, redraw and stability requirements on the qualified configuration; backup/restore and reproducible release build
Feature baseline agreed with Autodesk; no automatic import of later AutoCAD dimensioning, object-snap or 3D features

team environment / workstations: Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.

team environment / software: Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.

team environment / network: Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.

team environment / storage: The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.

team environment / support: Fund dedicated Autodesk engineering time, AION compiler/runtime and integration specialists, installation, training, documentation, replacement hardware, plotter access and on-site support through release. Retail onboarding/support-hour caps do not limit this separately sponsored agreement.

team environment / early graphics: January work uses available Artemis PRO displays and a stable software implementation of the graphics API. Supply 64 KiB/Color Pro engineering samples and mouse prototypes when qualified; do not make January work depend on the June professional hardware.

team environment / professional handover: Around June 1982 deliver the 128 KiB professional card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to the development and QA team, alongside the 64 KiB colour card/Color Pro 14 and mouse. This supersedes the earlier proposed January 17-inch prototype handover.

funding: Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective.

outcomes.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

professional hardware revision: COMDEX November revision adds explicit inherited modes, palette sequencing and five-sprite compatibility; preserve June development handover. See dated revisions in the catalog.

before.title: Birmingham funerals, inheritance and disposal of family assets
before.description: Operating as Adam Pleskot, Vincent spends 2 January to 2 February 1972 in Birmingham arranging the parents’ funeral, settling inheritance formalities and disposing of the family estate. After expenses he holds approximately GBP 6,000 and his remaining belongings for departure.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: The parents’ deaths and Vincent’s assumption of Adam’s identity create the need and opportunity to settle family affairs.
The estate includes the Birmingham house and saleable possessions, together with an insurance claim for the single family car destroyed in the fatal accident.

steps.description: Arrange the parents’ funeral.
Handle the formalities connected with inheriting the parents’ wealth.

Sell the house and saleable possessions, settle the insurance claim for the destroyed family car and receive its payout, handle any salvage formalities, and settle estate and funeral expenses. Retain approximately GBP 6,000 net and the remaining belongings for departure.

outcomes.description: The parents’ funeral has been arranged and inheritance formalities handled.

Adam holds approximately GBP 6,000 in net estate proceeds, including the crashed car’s insurance payout, and his remaining belongings after disposal and expenses. The car is not sold as a usable vehicle. The insurance amount is unspecified and is included in, rather than added to, the GBP 6,000 total.

before.title: Incorporation of Computer business
before.description: Adam establishes Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software and develops their initial leadership, engineering and software partnerships with DRI, BPI and others. This formation phase starts with the three companies on 23 November 1974 and ends with Tim Paterson’s recruitment.

participant.role: semiconductor research and development participant after its formation
software development participant after its formation

inputs.description: Adam’s established investment activity provides a financial basis for forming and supporting the computer businesses.
Adam contributes knowledge of future demand and technology while keeping its origin private.

steps.description: Establish and fund independent DRI as the operating-system cooperation partner.

Approach the prepared shortlist and recruit separate CEO, CFO and CTO roles for Logix Tech in San Jose, AION Labs in Cambridge, England, and AION Software in Copenhagen. Agree operating responsibilities and financial controls; individual appointees remain unspecified.
Establish the separate secret future-equipped facility supporting chip design.
Agree development and distribution cooperation with independent BPI Systems.
Recruit Gordon Letwin.

outcomes.description: Logix Tech, AION Labs and AION Software are established, with initial engineering infrastructure and supporting access to the separate future-equipped facility.
Cooperation with DRI and BPI is established under the existing agreements. DRI and BPI retain the independence and rights specified in those agreements.
Gordon Letwin and Tim Paterson have been recruited for the developing computer business.

before.title: Stepper procurement, installation and process development
before.description: From the January 1979 stepper order, procure and install the lithography equipment, record installation acceptance in September 1979, and coordinate DRAM yield-control and repair work plus 2.75 µm, 2.0 µm and 1.5 µm process and memory qualification through December 1983. Installation acceptance does not by itself qualify every process or product; existing processors retain their specified process until separately qualified.

inputs.description: The starting order authorises procurement; process development must meet measured tool-matching, retention, speed, yield and release gates rather than treating installation as production qualification.

outcomes.description: The programme records stepper acceptance, DRAM control and repair development, and the 2.75 µm, 2.0 µm and 1.5 µm qualification workstreams and release milestones. Individual capability transitions and part availability remain governed by their qualification records.

steps.description: Develop and qualify the dated manufacturing scenario; ERA1 remains on 3 µm. Budgets, yields and release gates are in memory_manufacturing.json.
Develop and qualify the 2.75 µm process and memory capabilities from July 1979 through June 1981.
Develop DRAM yield control and repair during the recorded 1980 workstream.
Record the improved 3 µm DRAM process-control release in June 1980, retaining its existing capability transition.
Develop the 2.0 µm process and RAM shrinks from January 1981 through December 1982.
Record the first complete 2.0 µm pilot lots in September 1981.
Develop and qualify the 1.5 µm process and RAM shrink from April 1982 through December 1983, including the recorded pilot and release milestones.

proposal.reason: Assign the agreed category to this top-level timeline record. Its child events and processes inherit the lane without storing their own categories.

before.title: Aurelia Foundation and Partnerships
before.description: Establish the commercial and partnership foundation for Aurelia: CP/M implementation, independent BPI cooperation, printer-mechanism supply, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support. Include the Aurelia launch campaign, NCC presentations, the start of BPI training and the dealer programme through the campaign’s end on 17 July 1978. The campaign hierarchy also owns recording, editing and free television distribution of cleared NCC material.

inputs.description: The established DRI partnership enables the Aurelia CP/M implementation agreement that starts this process.
Logix and AION provide the product, engineering and distribution organisation needed to negotiate and carry out the Aurelia partnerships.

outcomes.description: Aurelia has a partnership foundation covering CP/M implementation, OEM printer mechanisms, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support, as documented in the constituent events.

BPI pilot testing, launch qualification and dealer/instructor preparation support the launch of its independently owned Aurelia applications. Qualification gates and support limits remain those recorded in the milestones; BPI has accepted Adam’s investment and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment obligations, with future-platform work and a subsequent BPI share-buyback right.

steps.description: BPI accepts the investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement.
OEM printer-mechanism agreement.
ComputerLand retail agreement.
BPI business and accountant pilot programme.
Establish and prepare Logix Computer Academy through its dedicated launch-and-training process, from its founding event through 17 July 1978.
BPI and AION engineers tested the application family with businesses and accounting practices, reconciling its reports with existing records.
The partners checked posting, corrections, backup recovery, advertised payroll coverage and the summary export to Abacus.
BPI trained dealers and Academy instructors in the released configurations and its specialist-support arrangements before the June launch.

Run the Aurelia launch and Academy campaign through NCC presentations and the combined BPI training and dealer-programme opening on 17 July 1978. Prepare follow-up plans; completion of this campaign also completes the foundation process.

before.description: From 26 July 1978, prepare the products, technical cooperation and open-architecture programme associated with NCC 1979. participant.role: C platform, software and migration contributor
limited documentation and compatibility assistance partner

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch establishes the working platform, peripherals and software on which wider compatibility products and the next NCC programme build.

steps.description: Agree limited Apple technical cooperation on 8 February 1979, obtaining documentation, test equipment and compatibility assistance for native Apple expansion products.

Continue Logix-funded native Apple expansion development and compatibility testing, allowing independent compatible products. Apple retains its own peripheral strategy, does not manufacture FlexiBUS devices and does not adopt FlexiBUS as an official standard.
Execute campaign.ncc1979 through its existing campaign execution process, including preparation, NCC presentations and recorded follow-up.

outcomes.description: Apple II and S-100 expansion products have a recorded launch, and the campaign has presented documented compatibility and migration options with follow-up. Partner invitations and adoption targets remain distinct from signed commitments and measured results.
Limited Apple compatibility cooperation supports the native expansion work without committing Apple to manufacture FlexiBUS devices or adopt the Logix platform.

before.title: COMDEX 1979 campaign and presentation — execution
before.description: Prepare, present and follow up the Aurelia+ generation at COMDEX 1979, using the existing shared memory-development and Aurelia+ integration programmes for qualified launch configurations. Retain the campaign's dealer training, demonstrations, Academy follow-up and manufacturer workshops.

participant.role: shared memory development and integration qualification

inputs.description: The existing 120 person-month shared memory-development programme was completed by the third quarter of 1979, before this campaign begins. The existing 108 person-month Aurelia+ integration programme includes qualification; these are established programme allocations, not additional non-recurring engineering charges.

steps.description: Qualify the advertised Aurelia+ memory configuration for launch demonstrations and supported products using the existing integration programme.
activities / 0 / period: October–November 1979

activities / 0 / activity: Confidential dealer/BPI training, demo qualification, workflow rehearsal and press-material preparation. Invite business buyers and manufacturers to separate sessions; do not disclose unreleased specifications or pricing publicly.
activities / 1 / period: COMDEX launch week, December 1979

activities / 1 / activity: Trade-press demos and advertisements show side-by-side speed, charts and printed payslips. Press pack includes sample data/layouts, configurations and measured results. Paid broadcasting/celebrity promotion requires confirmed arrangements.
activities / 2 / period: At COMDEX
activities / 2 / activity: Business-workflow stations, existing-owner upgrade consultations, peripheral demos and manufacturer clinics. Each visitor gets a relevant next step.
activities / 3 / period: December 1979–January 1980
activities / 3 / activity: Dealer roadshows and Academy sessions: From spreadsheet to finished documents. Follow up with demonstrations and quotations.
activities / 4 / period: January–March 1980
activities / 4 / activity: Manufacturer porting workshops and publication of verified configuration-specific compatibility results.
Aurelia+, Pulse, Abacus 2.0 and manufacturer compatibility kit arrive
COMDEX 1979 dealer rehearsal and qualification
COMDEX 1979 dealer and Academy follow-up
Manufacturer porting workshops

before.title: Autodesk funded development and acceptance
before.description: Autodesk funded development and acceptance Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

inputs.description: The founders held an organising meeting on 30 January 1982. It provides the date basis and preparatory context for the agreement signed on 31 January, which starts this funded development programme. The source does not identify the meeting attendees.
Native AIONix/ERA build with reliable floating-point geometry and typed coordinate entry
Dual-display driver with colour command/status screen and 800x600 drawing canvas; independent palettes and explicit input focus
Explicit CAD mouse integration; standard TUI mouse support alone is insufficient
Drawing load/save and DXF exchange tests against the other supported AutoCAD builds
Supported pen-plotter output and physical drawing verification
Measured RAM, storage, redraw and stability requirements on the qualified configuration; backup/restore and reproducible release build
Feature baseline agreed with Autodesk; no automatic import of later AutoCAD dimensioning, object-snap or 3D features

team environment / workstations: Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.

team environment / software: Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.

team environment / network: Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.

team environment / storage: The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.

team environment / support: Fund dedicated Autodesk engineering time, AION compiler/runtime and integration specialists, installation, training, documentation, replacement hardware, plotter access and on-site support through release. Retail onboarding/support-hour caps do not limit this separately sponsored agreement.

team environment / early graphics: January work uses available Artemis PRO displays and a stable software implementation of the graphics API. Supply 64 KiB/Color Pro engineering samples and mouse prototypes when qualified; do not make January work depend on the June professional hardware.

team environment / professional handover: Around June 1982 deliver the 128 KiB professional card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to the development and QA team, alongside the 64 KiB colour card/Color Pro 14 and mouse. This supersedes the earlier proposed January 17-inch prototype handover.

funding: Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective.

outcomes.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.

professional hardware revision: COMDEX November revision adds explicit inherited modes, palette sequencing and five-sprite compatibility; preserve June development handover. See dated revisions in the catalog.

steps.description: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.
Meet programme acceptance gates; commercial shipment remains conditional on acceptance.

After incorporation on 26 April 1982, Autodesk adopts the founders' development arrangement, confirms source/porting rights and non-exclusive licensing, and reviews the compiler, recovery and graphics-driver milestones.
Milestone during this process: Professional 800x600 hardware becomes available to Autodesk.
Milestone during this process: AutoCAD Artemis beta and professional workflow qualification.

Build the ecosystem of independent manufacturers, software developers and peripheral contributors around Aurelia’s CP/M with TUI, FlexiBUS, C development interfaces, graphics subsystem and digital monitor connectivity. CP/M activity continues alongside the Artemis ecosystem phase; the envelope does not imply universal adoption or completion of all later targets.

participant.role: C development platform and application integration

inputs.description: Aurelia’s launch provides the working software, peripheral and display platform for independent implementations and supplier cooperation.
Use documented software APIs, bus rules, graphics profiles and monitor-link specifications, with explicit licensing and host-specific qualification.

outcomes.description: Independent contributors have a documented implementation and qualification programme covering CP/M/TUI, FlexiBUS, C development, graphics APIs and monitor connectivity. Final access terms and unverified participation remain subject to the existing agreements and qualification requirements.

The recorded milestones include portable DRI extension release, the supported Tandy configuration and initial qualified SMC chip sales. They do not establish release of every licensed chip or universal compatibility.
Microsoft BASIC has a recorded Aurelia release as independently licensed third-party software.

The closing market-response milestone records competition from bundled portable CP/M systems, making existing software libraries and total package cost important to business buyers without asserting alternative-world sales volumes or component supply.

Implement and qualify Tandy’s supported Model II CP/M, Abacus and FlexiBUS option without requiring Logix video hardware.
Begin external OEM implementations, documentation and qualification of portable CP/M extensions.
Release documented optional TUI, capability-discovery and FlexiBUS extensions for non-Logix manufacturers.
Microsoft releases licensed Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia at NCC 1979, contributing third-party language software to the ecosystem.

before.title: Ecosystem growth and market response — AIONix / 32-bit Artemis era
before.description: Coordinate ecosystem growth and market response for the AIONix and 32-bit Artemis phase from 1 May 1980 to 28 March 1982. Continue the independent implementation and supplier approach established in the CP/M phase, covering documented software interfaces, compatible products and non-ERA port feasibility. DRI’s 68k effort remains development and validation work rather than a released port or licence income.

participant.role: AIONix ownership, software interfaces and development platform
independently licensed non-ERA port feasibility and implementation

inputs.description: Supplier cooperation, documented interfaces and independent implementation practices established in the CP/M / 8-bit programme provide a foundation for the Artemis phase. CP/M ecosystem work continues alongside Artemis until April 1981; completion of the whole CP/M programme is not a prerequisite for Artemis work.
The completed AIONix development phase provides the operating-system foundation for Artemis-era integration and ecosystem work.

steps.description: Coordinate documented AIONix interfaces, developer access and compatible-product qualification while distinguishing supplier commitments, prototypes and released configurations.
Review selective native C/TUI application ports on 30 June 1980, testing files and arithmetic while retaining CP/M editions; source compatibility does not imply native execution of Z80 binaries.
Record independent vendors' interface-adapter qualification on 30 September 1980, including electrical and protocol conformance, supported configurations and optional AION certification.
Review 1980 sales, production capacity and investment on 31 December 1980, preserving the scenario's costed-production assumptions and 5% commercial capacity headroom.
Record the 31 July 1981 recession response: staged network purchases, leaner dealer stock and revised quarterly demand in place of uninterrupted monthly growth.
Record Unix suppliers' response on 15 October 1981, including mature tools, storage, support and software without assuming an instantly equivalent collaboration product.
Begin DRI’s independently licensed 68k AIONix port programme, including funded feasibility work, suitable external-MMU hardware assessment and restartable-fault investigation.

outcomes.description: The phase provides a framework for AIONix/Artemis ecosystem cooperation and records the start of DRI’s non-ERA port work. A completed 68k port, licence receipts and universal compatibility are not established by these activities.

before.title: Apple business-market response to Logix and AION
before.description: Apple responds to Logix and AION through software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, partner searches, Peachtree cooperation and business-system promotions. The recorded response runs from July 1978 through compatibility review and the Apple–Peachtree package opening on 15 March 1980. It does not imply an accelerated Lisa/GUI release or a nationwide training network.

participant.role: organiser of the competitive business-software and dealer response

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch and its integrated business-software demonstrations prompt Apple to strengthen its own software partnerships and business-dealer offering.

steps.description: Prepare selective business-dealer demonstrations, complete-system quotations and introductory customer lessons.
Expand the business-software initiative into searches and negotiations for independent accounting, spreadsheet and database partners.
Pursue the recorded Apple–Peachtree accounting cooperation while continuing separate spreadsheet and database efforts; retain the agreement’s existing negotiation status.
Promote complete Apple II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons.
Review successor-product compatibility requirements while retaining Apple’s independent roadmap.
Start the Apple–Peachtree small-business package with simplified setup, Apple II-oriented interaction, documentation and support.

outcomes.description: Apple has organised a coordinated response encompassing business-software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, Peachtree accounting cooperation and complete-configuration promotions. These activities establish no guaranteed sales, finished spring-1979 package or nationwide training network.
Apple has reviewed compatibility requirements for successor products, prioritising protection of existing software, peripherals and customer data while retaining its independent hardware roadmap.

The Apple–Peachtree small-business package has a recorded start with simplified setup, documentation and support. The event’s possible accounting-module coverage remains qualified rather than a guarantee of every module.

before.description: From the confidential market investigation on 5 July 1979, IBM develops Project Chess in response to Logix, Tandy, Apple and independent software suppliers. Project authorisation, OS sourcing review, substitute OS funding and qualification delays lead to the independently commissioned disk-OS platform launch on the scenario date of 15 March 1982, conditional on qualification.

participant.role: market investigation, PC project sponsor and software qualification lead

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch establishes the competing business-computing platform and workflows IBM subsequently benchmarks.
Assess competing applications, interfaces, distribution, training, service and independent OS suppliers before committing the project’s delivery approach.

steps.description: Authorise IBM’s personal-computer project in response to independent suppliers’ business applications and channels.
Review software sourcing and identify the gap between available OS options and the required schedule.
Fund an alternative OS delivery programme and stabilise application interfaces while hardware development continues.
Record OS integration, application qualification and support delays; keep the projected commercial release distinct from a confirmed launch.

Consider the protected-x86 feasibility context recorded by DRI after 80286 availability. Segmentation, tools, hardware and validation remain unresolved; this does not establish IBM adoption of AIONix or an immediate 286 release.

outcomes.description: The process culminates in the recorded alternative IBM business-PC launch with an independently commissioned disk OS and an initially narrower application portfolio. The 15 March 1982 date remains the central scenario conditional on qualification; the supplier and OS name remain unspecified.

before.title: Birmingham funerals, inheritance and disposal of family assets
before.description: Operating as Adam Pleskot, Vincent spends 2 January to 2 February 1972 in Birmingham arranging the parents’ funeral, settling inheritance formalities and disposing of the family estate. After expenses he holds approximately GBP 6,000 and his remaining belongings for departure.

participant.role: protagonist; Vincent operating as Adam Pleskot after the identity takeover

inputs.description: The parents’ deaths and Vincent’s assumption of Adam’s identity create the need and opportunity to settle family affairs.
The estate includes the Birmingham house and saleable possessions, together with an insurance claim for the single family car destroyed in the fatal accident.

steps.description: Arrange the parents’ funeral.
Handle the formalities connected with inheriting the parents’ wealth.

Sell the house and saleable possessions, settle the insurance claim for the destroyed family car and receive its payout, handle any salvage formalities, and settle estate and funeral expenses. Retain approximately GBP 6,000 net and the remaining belongings for departure.

outcomes.description: The parents’ funeral has been arranged and inheritance formalities handled.

Adam holds approximately GBP 6,000 in net estate proceeds, including the crashed car’s insurance payout, and his remaining belongings after disposal and expenses. The car is not sold as a usable vehicle. The insurance amount is unspecified and is included in, rather than added to, the GBP 6,000 total.

proposal.title: AION Labs manufacturing establishment and maturation — six-stage programme
proposal.reason: Author-requested manufacturing programme: six overlapping subprocesses, role-based hires, direct predecessor inputs, technology/capability outputs and separate product maturity gates. New dates are proposed scenario choices for whole-group review. Preserve existing launch and stepper milestones; enrich and reparent the existing stepper programme instead of duplicating it. The 1983 parent end contains its existing shrink work. Mask-ROM is a scoped logic recipe within the existing schema. Correct the unrepairable launch DRAM criterion so repair is not backdated. Apply all elements atomically; existing authorizations and foundation records remain unchanged until approval.

after.name: AION wafer traceability, process control and yield engineering
after.description: Control of the Cambridge fabrication line through traceable lots, measured process windows, failure analysis and controlled recipe changes.

specification.description: Trace each wafer to material batch, tool, operator, recipe revision and electrical results; map defects and distinguish random from systematic failures.
Monitor particles, film thickness, sheet resistance, transistor thresholds, contacts and tool drift; use control charts and documented corrective action.
Separate engineering lots from released production; qualify maintenance and tool substitutions before customer manufacture.
Report wafer completion, electrical die yield, accepted speed/retention bins, package yield and good saleable chips per wafer separately.

after.name: AION memory characterisation and production testing
after.description: Wafer-probe, packaged-device and reliability tests supporting separate ROM, SRAM and DRAM release decisions.

specification.description: Qualify ROM image verification and SRAM read/write margins separately from DRAM retention, sensing, refresh and disturb behaviour.
Test across specified voltage and temperature limits; retain lot histories, wafer maps and failure-analysis evidence.
For repairable DRAM revisions, map defects, programme only supported redundancy and retest the complete device; unrepairable launch revisions receive no assumed repair benefit.

after.name: AION 3 µm customer-specific mask-ROM manufacture
after.description: Mask-ROM product recipe within the silicon-gate NMOS logic family; ROM-specific qualification does not qualify arbitrary logic or CPUs.

qualification_requirements.description: Customer-approved image, organisation, mask revision, package, timing and supply contract.
Repeatable wafer probe, full image verification, packaged test and reliability across independent lots.
Released order-specific masks and acceptance before customer shipments.

after.name: AION 3 µm SRAM manufacture
after.description: Small SRAM product-family capability, beginning with a 1 Kbit design and evaluating a separately qualified 4 Kbit extension.

qualification_requirements.description: Release each density, pinout, package and speed grade separately.
Read/write, standby leakage, data-pattern and voltage/temperature margins verified on multiple lots.
Production test coverage, package reliability and recurring cost per accepted chip.

after.name: AION 3 µm 16 Kbit DRAM manufacture
after.description: Cambridge recipe for the AION 4116-equivalent; production release precedes the June 1978 Aurelia launch.

qualification_requirements.description: Qualify capacitor, sense amplifiers, retention, disturb patterns and refresh across temperature and voltage.
Release 16-pin package, +12/+5/-5 V supplies, sequencing and measured speed grades against the product contract.
Demonstrate repeatable results across independent wafer lots, packaged final test and reliability screening.

after.name: AION 3 µm ERAv1 manufacture
after.description: Processor-specific fabrication, test and packaging capability. Initial release covers the 6 MHz part; 8 MHz requires separate measured qualification.

qualification_requirements.description: Frozen design rules, die and mask revisions, package/pinout, rails and power contract.
Functional vectors, timing across voltage/temperature, reliability and repeatable independent lots.
Record whether 6/8 MHz are speed bins or separate revisions; release only demonstrated grades.
Qualified launch inventory and production capacity before 19 May 1980; no dependence on later DRAM-control or sub-3 µm releases.

after.title: AION Labs manufacturing establishment and maturation
after.description: Establish Cambridge fabrication from the 1974 founding, develop commercial memory and repeatable 3 µm manufacture, qualify ERAv1 for the 1980 launch, and continue the existing stepper-led maturation through 1983. Adam funds capital and development; memory sales support operating costs without an assumed self-financing ramp.

inputs.description: The founding establishes AION Labs and its semiconductor investment mandate.

steps.description: 1. Establish the manufacturing team and pilot line.
2. Qualify commercial mask-ROM and SRAM manufacture.
3. Develop and qualify 16 Kbit DRAM.
4. Establish repeatable yield control and manufacturing discipline.
5. Develop 64 Kbit DRAM and continue the existing stepper programme.
6. Qualify 3 µm ERAv1 production for the 1980 launch.

outcomes.description: Cambridge process-control and test methods support separately qualified logic, ROM, SRAM and DRAM recipes.
The existing stepper programme delivers its separately dated smaller-geometry qualification outcomes.

after.title: Cambridge manufacturing team and pilot-line establishment
after.description: Recruit manufacturing leadership and establish a 75 mm silicon-gate NMOS pilot line with a 3 µm qualification objective. Use forgiving test structures during equipment bring-up.

inputs.description: AION Labs exists and can appoint staff and fund the Cambridge facility.

steps.description: Appoint the experienced manufacturing leadership and core integration team.
Purchase clean-area systems, ultrapure water, filtered gases, chemical handling and reliable temperature-controlled utilities.

Purchase and install Micralign projection lithography, resist coating/development, oxidation and diffusion furnaces, silicon/dielectric deposition, wet processing, metallisation, inspection and wafer probing.

Seek a licensed silicon-gate NMOS process-transfer package with training, design rules, test structures and reference wafers. Qualify the actual Cambridge route; a supplier or licence is not assumed from recruitment alone.
Hire equipment-maintenance, facilities, contamination-control and test technicians; contract supplier installation and training support.
Qualify 75 mm wafer handling and test structures; document process windows, tool acceptance and pilot electrical results.

outcomes.description: An accepted pilot line and documented process route support separate product qualification.

after.title: AION appoints its Cambridge manufacturing team
after.description: AION appoints a fab director, silicon-gate NMOS integration lead, lithography lead, facilities lead and test/reliability lead with production-ramp experience. Recruitment draws on established British, European and US semiconductor operations; individual names and former employers are unspecified. Supplier engineers train the new staff.

inputs.description: The founding authorises recruitment and investment.

outcomes.description: The appointed team takes responsibility for defining and qualifying the Cambridge process and its controls.

after.title: Cambridge 75 mm NMOS pilot line accepted
after.description: The team accepts the installed line and repeatable test-structure operation. Pilot acceptance establishes engineering capability, not commercial product release.

inputs.description: The appointed team commissions equipment, trains operators and verifies the pilot route.

outcomes.description: Pilot recipes, wafer traceability and tool-acceptance evidence are available.
Cambridge 75 mm NMOS pilot line accepted — pilot

after.title: Commercial mask-ROM and small-SRAM qualification
after.description: Use customer-specific mask ROM and a modest SRAM family to establish repeatable fabrication, customer acceptance and an operating-revenue base. Sales quantities, prices and profitability remain unspecified.

inputs.description: The accepted pilot line can run product engineering lots.

steps.description: Hire ROM/SRAM product and applications engineers and a commercial lead for industrial controllers, instrumentation, terminals and peripherals.
Develop customer-specific mask ROM and a 1 Kbit SRAM; evaluate 4 Kbit SRAM only as a separate product qualification. Charge for ROM design/masks and seek minimum-order commitments.
Pursue licensed second-source contracts with explicit process-transfer, test, sales-right and customer-acceptance terms; no unexecuted licence or guaranteed customer demand is counted as income.
Install automated probing, memory testing, temperature fixtures and reliability ovens; initially qualify external assembly suppliers and retain AION final-test responsibility.
Qualify independent wafer lots and customer-approved ROM images, packages, timing and SRAM margins.

outcomes.description: Released mask-ROM and initial SRAM recipes provide commercial manufacturing experience and product-specific test methods.

after.title: AION releases initial mask-ROM and SRAM manufacture
after.description: Independent lots meet the selected ROM and 1 Kbit SRAM contracts. AION releases qualified order-specific ROMs and the initial SRAM grade for customer supply; the 4 Kbit extension and second-source licences require separate acceptance.

inputs.description: Product lots build on the accepted Cambridge pilot process.

outcomes.description: ROM/SRAM electrical, package and test evidence supports the released scope.
AION releases initial mask-ROM and SRAM manufacture — production released
AION releases initial mask-ROM and SRAM manufacture — production released

after.title: 16 Kbit DRAM development and production qualification
after.description: Build a dedicated DRAM team, establish capacitor and sense-amplifier behaviour with small test arrays, and qualify AION 4116-equivalent production before Aurelia launches in June 1978.

inputs.description: The pilot fab provides the platform for DRAM-specific process development.

steps.description: Recruit DRAM device, sensing and memory-test specialists.
Purchase ion implantation and annealing capability, and qualify the deposition/patterning sequence required by the selected capacitor structure.
Use small arrays or a 4 Kbit engineering vehicle to isolate leakage, sensing and refresh faults; an intermediate commercial release is not required.
Develop the 16 Kbit array and sensing circuits; qualify retention, disturb behaviour, supply sequencing, package and timing.
Extend temperature-controlled wafer and packaged testing, reliability screening and failure analysis; prove repeatability across independent lots.

outcomes.description: The 16 Kbit DRAM recipe and memory-test methods support Aurelia supply.

after.title: AION recruits DRAM process and test specialists
after.description: AION recruits a DRAM integration lead, capacitor/device engineer, sense-amplifier designer and memory-test lead with production experience. Offers include relocation, equipment budgets and long-term incentives. No named employee, former employer or proprietary transfer is presumed.

inputs.description: The operating pilot line gives the recruited specialists an executable development platform.

outcomes.description: Specialists establish the DRAM recipe and its retention, refresh and test requirements.

after.title: AION 16 Kbit DRAM production qualified
after.description: Independent lots of the AION 4116-equivalent meet released retention, refresh, timing, supply, package and reliability limits. The release supports manufacturing and inventory preparation for June 1978; no numeric yield is asserted.

inputs.description: The specialist team develops the DRAM recipe and verifies the production qualification lots.

outcomes.description: The released 16 Kbit DRAM process includes controlled recipes and complete production-test evidence.
AION 16 Kbit DRAM production qualified — production released

after.title: Cambridge yield engineering and production control
after.description: Turn recurring ROM/SRAM production into a controlled factory process, then extend the controls to separately qualified DRAM. Protect customer manufacture from experimental recipe changes.

inputs.description: Recurring qualified product lots provide failure maps and operational evidence for yield improvement.

steps.description: Appoint the permanent yield, failure-analysis and maintenance group.
Purchase film-thickness, sheet-resistance and transistor measurement equipment, improved inspection, and scanning-electron-microscope access; link wafer maps to lot histories.
Improve cleaning, filtration, gas purity, contamination monitoring and preventive maintenance; stock spares and duplicate bottleneck tools where justified.
Qualify plasma stripping and selected dry-etch operations layer by layer, controlling damage, residues and dimensions.
Run controlled experiments on implants, oxidation, annealing and contacts. Release improvements only after independent production lots pass electrical and reliability limits.
Measure wafer completion, electrical yield, accepted bins, package yield, good chips per wafer and recurring cost separately; do not count forecast yields as observed results.

outcomes.description: Repeatable 3 µm logic manufacture and controlled ROM/SRAM/DRAM routes support subsequent product ramps.

after.title: AION establishes a permanent yield-engineering group
after.description: AION appoints a yield manager, failure-analysis engineer, process-control engineers and maintenance specialists with authority to hold suspect lots and reject uncontrolled recipe changes.

inputs.description: Commercial lot histories establish the immediate need for systematic yield engineering.

outcomes.description: The team owns traceability, defect analysis, process windows and corrective-action methods.

after.title: Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production
after.description: Independent logic test vehicles and released memory lots demonstrate controlled electrical distributions and stable production procedures. Product-specific timing, retention and package qualifications remain separate; no universal yield percentage is assigned.

inputs.description: The yield group establishes and verifies the production controls.
Released 16 Kbit production supplies the DRAM evidence needed for this cross-recipe review.

outcomes.description: Process-control evidence supports the separately scoped Cambridge production recipes.
Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production — repeatable production
Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production — repeatable production
Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production — repeatable production
Cambridge demonstrates repeatable 3 µm production — repeatable production

after.title: 64 Kbit DRAM and stepper-led manufacturing maturation
after.description: Develop the initial 3 µm 64 Kbit DRAM for December 1979 and coordinate its later maturation with the existing stepper programme. The launch recipe, 1980 process controls, 1981 repair and later shrinks retain separate qualifications.

inputs.description: The qualified 16 Kbit recipe and specialist team provide the immediate basis for the 64 Kbit development.

steps.description: Develop the larger array, capacitor, sense amplifiers, refresh and production tests on the existing 3 µm route; run engineering lots before stepper installation.
Complete engineering lots and review the initial 64 Kbit design.
Release qualified launch silicon before Aurelia+.
Execute the existing stepper procurement and process-development programme, including its established DRAM-control, repair and shrink workstreams.
Build qualified launch inventory and preserve existing customer supply during experiments; select later shrink recipes by measured packaged-chip cost and reliability.

outcomes.description: Initial 64 Kbit DRAM manufacture and separately dated control, repair and shrink capabilities support successive products.

after.title: AION completes initial 64 Kbit DRAM pilot lots
after.description: Engineering lots establish the initial 3 µm 64 Kbit array, sensing and refresh behaviour. Retention, speed, package and reliability work continues before release. This revision has no assumed redundancy repair.

inputs.description: The qualified smaller DRAM supplies the device and process starting point.
The demonstrated process controls support larger-die pilot fabrication.

outcomes.description: Pilot results and defect maps guide the launch-recipe corrections.
AION completes initial 64 Kbit DRAM pilot lots — pilot

after.title: AION releases its initial 3 µm 64 Kbit DRAM
after.description: Multiple independent lots meet the launch contract for retention, refresh, timing, rails, package and reliability. Release supports inventory for December 1979 Aurelia+ and reuse in Artemis; later control and repair revisions confer no early yield benefit.

inputs.description: Pilot failures and electrical results are resolved and verified in qualification lots.

outcomes.description: The initial 64 Kbit production recipe and full test contract are released.
AION releases its initial 3 µm 64 Kbit DRAM — production released

after.title: ERAv1 3 µm manufacturing and launch qualification

specification.description: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.

specification.description: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
specification.value: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.

specification.description: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.

before.title: Apple business-market response to Logix and AION
before.description: Apple responds to Logix and AION through software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, partner searches, Peachtree cooperation and business-system promotions. The recorded response runs from July 1978 through compatibility review and the Apple–Peachtree package opening on 15 March 1980. It does not imply an accelerated Lisa/GUI release or a nationwide training network.

participant.role: organiser of the competitive business-software and dealer response

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch and its integrated business-software demonstrations prompt Apple to strengthen its own software partnerships and business-dealer offering.

steps.description: Prepare selective business-dealer demonstrations, complete-system quotations and introductory customer lessons.
Expand the business-software initiative into searches and negotiations for independent accounting, spreadsheet and database partners.
Pursue the recorded Apple–Peachtree accounting cooperation while continuing separate spreadsheet and database efforts; retain the agreement’s existing negotiation status.
Promote complete Apple II business configurations, demonstrations and introductory lessons.
Review successor-product compatibility requirements while retaining Apple’s independent roadmap.
Start the Apple–Peachtree small-business package with simplified setup, Apple II-oriented interaction, documentation and support.

outcomes.description: Apple has organised a coordinated response encompassing business-software recruitment, selective dealer demonstrations, Peachtree accounting cooperation and complete-configuration promotions. These activities establish no guaranteed sales, finished spring-1979 package or nationwide training network.

inputs.description: The Artemis commercial launch provides the platform to extend with networked business and server configurations.

steps.description: Develop and integrate TCP/IP networking, AIONix server services and supported Aurelia/Artemis network upgrades.

proposal.title: Separate BPI, DRI, Microsoft and Tandy offerings; retain the Logix CP/M cartridge
proposal.reason: Move third-party commercial identities to descriptive external products while preserving direct technical relationships. Shared records and dependent removals are grouped so approval is atomic. External records were imported separately as Pending authorization; approval of this proposal does not authorize them. No dates, process ownership, categories or launch assignments change. Retain the Logix CP/M cartridge and distinguish the licensed Aurelia software from portable DRI extensions. Consolidate BPI package aliases without deleting their implementation editions. Revised under the reference rules: prerequisites and technical resources use explained inputs; deliveries, decisions and qualification use explained outcomes; loose and inherited subject lists are removed. Explicit launch/announcement or later-promotion associations remain only where no canonical reverse relationship exists. No dates, ownership, categories, launch assignments or current foundation records are changed.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Build the ecosystem of independent manufacturers, software developers and peripheral contributors around Aurelia’s CP/M with TUI, FlexiBUS, C development interfaces, graphics subsystem and digital monitor connectivity. Coordinate documented implementation and qualification, SMC second-source transfer, portable DRI extensions and Tandy cooperation. CP/M activity continues alongside the Artemis ecosystem phase; the envelope does not imply universal adoption or completion of all later targets.

outcomes.description: Independent contributors have a documented implementation and qualification programme covering CP/M/TUI, FlexiBUS, C development, graphics APIs and monitor connectivity. The recorded milestones include portable DRI extension release, the supported Tandy configuration and initial qualified SMC chip sales. They do not establish release of every licensed chip or universal compatibility.

The closing market-response milestone records competition from bundled portable CP/M systems, making existing software libraries and total package cost important to business buyers without asserting alternative-world sales volumes or component supply.

message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, tuition, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified and separately quoted.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material free of charge to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix covers normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.
