before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
before.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
claim_policy: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

stage.label: Customer choice
stage.description: Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

stage.label: Applications across computers
stage.description: Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

stage.label: Business applications
stage.description: Demonstrate Abacus, then independent BPI records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that BPI has a Model II port.

stage.label: FlexiBUS peripherals
stage.description: Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

stage.label: Apple II and S-100 expansion products
stage.description: Present the Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II alongside the S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative joins the native Apple demonstration. Explain the drivers, optional display hardware and separate S-100 support without suggesting Apple endorses S-100 systems.

stage.label: Independent partners
stage.description: DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

stage.label: Preparing for the next generation
stage.description: Adam explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

stage.label: Availability and next steps
stage.description: Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_content.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

marketing_content.type: Apple II and S-100 product sheet
marketing_content.description: The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit.

Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent BPI branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 50 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
before.description: Prepare the compatibility programme and partner demonstrations, deliver the NCC 1979 presentation and expansion-product launch, then run recruitment, dealer activity and qualification follow-up through the January 1980 review. Campaign.ncc1979 supplies the messages, presentation and marketing materials.

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch provides the working platform and business applications used to prepare cross-vendor demonstrations.
The Tandy cooperation agreement provides the basis for the Model II prototype and application-interchange work.
The limited Apple cooperation agreement provides documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II products.

Prepare named configurations, host-specific drivers, documented transfer paths and measured resource limits. Protect future architecture information and clear partner participation before public demonstrations.

outcomes.description: Published compatibility profiles, implementation guidance and records of unresolved access and support terms.
Rehearsed demonstration configurations, interoperability test records and an issue register distinguishing verified behaviour from limitations.
The NCC presentation and expansion-product launch have been delivered, with native Apple and S-100 support described separately and partner responsibilities retained.

An updated compatibility directory, recruitment and qualification records, dealer and developer materials, and an evidence-based closing review. Adoption and sales targets are not treated as achieved outcomes.

steps.description: Evaluate recruitment prospects and engineering kits. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration or distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Preserve existing applications and display investment; interest does not constitute an agreement.

Treat North Star and Vector as strong CP/M prospects with moderately strong FlexiBUS prospects; optional Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Cromemco is a moderate CP/M and FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its own OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited Logix-video potential; no platform redesign is assumed. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential, with limited Logix-video interest; plan late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification, not June availability. Heath/Heathkit has moderate CP/M and host-specific FlexiBUS potential but limited Logix-video interest; treat it as later feasibility work, not a promised 1979 release. These assessments guide outreach and do not establish commitments.
Publish compatibility profiles and provide reference-driver and test access alongside the separate DRI extension release. Record unresolved commercial and support terms.

Prepare the presentation space, audiovisual equipment and qualified demonstration systems. Test document round trips, disk formats, memory limits, loading, recalculation and device behaviour. Review all public material for the embargo and secure partner clearance.
Run supplier workshops, test named configurations and record failures and required corrections before public demonstrations.
Deliver the NCC presentation and the combined Apple II/S-100 expansion-product launch using the approved campaign materials and qualified systems.
Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Maintain a directory that distinguishes shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.
Update availability evidence for the separately recorded Tandy release and individually qualified SMC and peripheral products. Keep future products out of shipping claims.
Review progress against the campaign’s adoption targets using verified OEM configurations, qualifications and third-party device availability.

Track compatible-computer sell-through across vendors, qualified application editions, peripheral shipments and supported device classes, document-interchange results, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Count distinct manufacturers rather than duplicate dealer builds or SKUs.

Prepare the closing review with verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Report progress toward NCC 1980 goals without claiming unverified results or disclosing future architecture.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
before.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
claim_policy: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

stage.label: Customer choice
stage.description: Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

stage.label: Applications across computers
stage.description: Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

stage.label: Business applications
stage.description: Demonstrate Abacus, then independent BPI records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that BPI has a Model II port.

stage.label: FlexiBUS peripherals
stage.description: Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

stage.label: Apple II and S-100 expansion products
stage.description: Present the Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II alongside the S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative joins the native Apple demonstration. Explain the drivers, optional display hardware and separate S-100 support without suggesting Apple endorses S-100 systems.

stage.label: Independent partners
stage.description: DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

stage.label: Preparing for the next generation
stage.description: Adam explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

stage.label: Availability and next steps
stage.description: Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_content.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

marketing_content.type: Apple II and S-100 product sheet
marketing_content.description: The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit.

Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent BPI branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 50 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

before.title: Aurelia+, Pulse, Abacus 2.0 and manufacturer compatibility kit arrive
before.description: Launches Aurelia+. Presents Pulse and Abacus 2.0. Makes corresponding training available. Launch the Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit with published contracts, reference runtime adapters, diagnostics and application acceptance tests. Manufacturers may independently implement the released environment; optional paid support and certification use standard terms. Application redistribution remains separately licensed. Shift new hardware development and promotion to Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones. Continue installed-base support and compatible software; do not impose an immediate Aurelia withdrawal. FlexiBUS and Logix video adoption remain separate choices. Future architecture details remain undisclosed until NCC 1980. Present the 45-minute COMDEX campaign plus questions: More room to work. More freedom to choose. Run identical live calculated shaded-cube and Abacus workloads on Aurelia and Aurelia+ under equivalent conditions; show measured results without an unverified speed multiplier. See comdex_1979_campaign.json. Demonstrate Abacus 2.0 charts and spreadsheet-linked layouts using precalculated fictitious employee values, then preview and print a complete payslip batch. The head of independent BPI follows Abacus with the source payroll and reconciled file-exchange workflow, and joins the partner segment. Abacus 2.0 also serves existing Aurelia owners.

participant.role: independent partner; head of BPI presents

inputs.description: The later BPI partner presentation supplies source payroll and reconciled file-exchange data for the Abacus demonstration; this is a repeat promotion and workflow dependency, not BPI’s original launch.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy — execution
before.description: From 26 March to 17 July 1978, Logix coordinates the Aurelia launch campaign, qualified demonstrations and NCC presentations, ending when the combined BPI training, direct-sales and dealer programme begins. The campaign also prepares undated follow-up plans for year-end workshops and customer-led expansion; these plans do not assert completion of later work by July.

inputs.description: The Academy’s establishment on 25 March provides the training organisation and preparation basis for the campaign that begins the next day.

outcomes.description: Attractively edited broadcast feature with a clear business-user narrative
Short station-ready news packages and demonstration excerpts
Clean footage, separate narration/audio where practical, accurate captions and a factual product/Academy press sheet
Full edited presentations for stations wanting longer technical coverage

Aurelia and independent BPI applications have been presented at NCC; BPI training, direct sales and dealer qualification have begun. Follow-up plans cover year-end preparation, module upgrades and expansion based on verified customer results.

steps.description: Cinematic TV commercial and explanatory print advertisements; prioritise markets with demonstration, support and Academy coverage.
Coordinate the teaser, advertising, press and dealer preparation, then the nested NCC launch, technical sessions and media activities.

Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims.

Qualify all advertised launch modules and a modest summary export to Abacus. Train instructors and dealers, publish requirements and support boundaries, and prepare a joint press preview. Measured capacity and final jurisdiction coverage remain acceptance gates, not invented results.

Prepare the following follow-up programme: Run year-end preparation workshops and module-upgrade demonstrations. Specify payroll update coverage and maintenance terms. Customer data remains under customer control; referrals do not imply an accountant endorsement without consent.

Prepare the following follow-up programme: Expand demonstrations and qualified support using verified customer results. Promote module-to-suite upgrade credit. BPI Model II support is a separate future negotiation; the existing Tandy agreement covers Abacus only.

After NCC, edit the recorded material into the broadcast feature, station-ready news/demo excerpts, clean captioned footage and press sheet, and full edited presentations listed in the outcomes. Offer cleared, Logix-identified material free of charge to any willing television station, covering normal duplication, dispatch and station-compatible copies. Distribute as editing and clearances are completed; delivery dates and runtimes remain production decisions. Station participation, scheduling and editorial selection are voluntary: no guaranteed airtime, compulsory advertising purchase or implied endorsement.

proposal.title: Phase 7: Resolve Artemis offerings and launch Hard-Disk Office at COMDEX 1980
proposal.reason: Revised following author feedback: introduce product.artemis_budget_128_hdd at COMDEX on 19 November 1980, not the NCC Artemis launch, because the Seagate ST506 is unavailable for the earlier configuration. Point the product to campaign.comdex1980 and event.software32, remove the pre-COMDEX composition, and retain two revisions: COMDEX launch with optional Abacus 3, then the May 1981 network option with separately selected compatible software. Number these revisions 1 and 2; no live record pins the previously proposed versions. Remove HDD claims from the Artemis launch description, outcome and NCC execution step. Describe the actual introduction in the COMDEX campaign, process and launch event, removing its now-redundant reverse product subject. Preserve the rest of this proposal: AIONix C IDE and the single replacement RAM module launch at NCC 1980, the erroneous 1978 IDE association is removed, technical details remain canonical, and Academy pricing/source-file wording is cleaned up. Shared whole-record edits remain one atomic proposal. Existing event dates, process periods and technical device definitions stay unchanged; release timing does not assert successful engineering qualification.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
before.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

stage.label: partners
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: academy
stage.description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates once finalised. BPI-authorised courses and the dealer programme start July 17; specialist support is provided by BPI.

stage.label: packages
stage.description: State complete package contents, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training and setup arrangements.

stage.label: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem
stage.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

stage.label: Aurelia C compiler Integrated Development Environment and SDK
stage.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

stage.label: premiere / venue
stage.description: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.

stage.label: premiere / stages / 7 / description

before.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
before.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required. Logix introduced an Artemis 128 KiB office configuration with two floppy drives, a Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support. A second configuration added a 5 MB disk subsystem. Customers could add Abacus 3 from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.

before.title: Artemis platform launches commercially
before.description: Launch Artemis with AIONix, peripherals, expansions, developer tooling and support. Introduces Artemis training. At NCC 1980 reveal the processor architecture and word size withheld in the NCC 1979 public campaign. The separately sold Z80 compatibility module is an optional qualified legacy path; native applications require an appropriate target build. Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path. Demonstrate familiar multitasking, separate ERA/Z80 C builds and qualified legacy-card execution; compare verified vector calculations on Aurelia+, PDP-11/34 and Artemis before revealing the 32-bit RISC ERA 1 architecture. Publish only measured performance. The head of independent BPI Systems presents after Abacus and joins the partner section; BPI retains separate branding, licences, support and receipts. Ship Artemis 128 with a replaceable 16 KiB video card and Mono II or Color II; ship Artemis 256 with 32 AION 64 Kbit system RAM chips, a 32 KiB video card and Mono Pro or Color II. Both cards include 1 KiB exclusive sprite SRAM. Only the professional card and Mono Pro enable 640×400 modes; Color II keeps legacy timings. High-resolution demonstrations and paid follow-up campaign are separately budgeted; production qualification remains required. Logix introduced an Artemis 128 KiB office configuration with two floppy drives, a Color Monitor II, keyboard, AIONix, Business Tools and one year of support. A second configuration added a 5 MB disk subsystem. Customers could add Abacus 3 from November 1980 and networking from May 1981.

before.title: Aurelia+, Pulse, Abacus 2.0 and manufacturer compatibility kit arrive
before.description: Launches Aurelia+. Presents Pulse and Abacus 2.0. Makes corresponding training available. Launch the Aurelia Software Compatibility Kit with published contracts, reference runtime adapters, diagnostics and application acceptance tests. Manufacturers may independently implement the released environment; optional support and certification use standard terms. Application redistribution remains separately licensed. Shift new hardware development and promotion to Aurelia+ while enabling independent Aurelia-class clones. Continue installed-base support and compatible software; do not impose an immediate Aurelia withdrawal. FlexiBUS and Logix video adoption remain separate choices. Future architecture details remain undisclosed until NCC 1980. Present the 45-minute COMDEX campaign plus questions: More room to work. More freedom to choose. Run identical live calculated shaded-cube and Abacus workloads on Aurelia and Aurelia+ under equivalent conditions; show measured results without an unverified speed multiplier. See comdex_1979_campaign.json. Demonstrate Abacus 2.0 charts and spreadsheet-linked layouts using precalculated fictitious employee values, then preview and print a complete payslip batch. The head of independent BPI follows Abacus with the source payroll and reconciled file-exchange workflow, and joins the partner segment. Abacus 2.0 also serves existing Aurelia owners.

proposal.title: Date device revisions from their earliest supported use
proposal.reason: Derive first use through version-pinned product composition paths, including use inside another device. End final versions at the 1995-01-01 simulation cutoff. Professional 128 KiB graphics and Mono Pro 17 revision 1 begin at the June 1982 Autodesk engineering handover (month precision retained), and revision 2 begins at their 1982-11-29 COMDEX commercial launch; this is a proposed revision assignment, not proof of qualification. One unused technical definition, the Aurelia 16 KB RAM expansion card, has no dated use in the graph: retain its unknown start and raise a focused discussion instead of inventing a launch. Base parts have no composition history in this schema; no dates are added to their definitions.

before.name: Logix Aurelia 16 KB RAM expansion card
before.description: Optional 16 KB RAM card occupying one Plug and Execute expansion slot. On Aurelia it increases installed RAM from 48 KB to 64 KB. The mapper exposes its four 4 KB pages at B000–EFFF in the normal application view; ROM and video RAM can temporarily overlay those pages without erasing their contents.

memory_mapping.configuration: Firmware discovers the card at startup and maps its pages; no manual address switches.
memory_mapping.system_workspace: The existing 4 KB common system RAM remains at F000–FFFF; the card adds 16 KB to lower RAM.
memory_mapping.service_calls: The common-memory runtime saves the RAM mapping, selects ROM/video RAM for a service and restores the card pages before returning.
memory_mapping.installation: Install with power off, then restart so firmware can discover and test the card.
memory_mapping.application_memory: Lower RAM rises from 44 KB to 60 KB, before other system and workspace reservations.

physical_population.refresh_owner: Host memory controller must refresh the card even while its pages are overlaid; exact interface pending.

adapter_requirements.buffer_policy: Local adapter RAM, additional to host system RAM. Partition transmit/receive buffers and metadata; freeze maximum frame length and IP MTU to fit complete frames before implementation. Physical RAM chip count remains unresolved.
adapter_requirements.flow_control: Grant unicast only when the destination advertises credit for a complete frame; reserve that credit until completion. Use flow control first for receiver pressure, not automatic rate changes.
adapter_requirements.host_service: No per-byte interrupt requirement. Aurelia at 250 kbit/s has 128 CPU clocks per raw byte at 4 MHz; Aurelia+ at 500 kbit/s has 96 at 6 MHz. Validate worst-case service latency. A persistently slow host may advertise a lower configured ceiling.

before.name: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card
before.description: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

requirements.description: Dedicated slot; powered-off replacement only; host interface, power rails and signal integrity require qualification.
Qualification pending.

before.name: Logix Artemis Professional 128 KiB video card
before.description: Logix Artemis Professional 128 KiB video card

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.memory_policy: 11072 bytes remain for bounded scratch/cursor work; allocations must be accounted for. No second framebuffer or inherited five-sprite subsystem is promised.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
specification.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
specification.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
specification.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
specification.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

before.name: Logix Mono Pro 17
before.description: Logix Mono Pro 17

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Qualify revised deflection, analog grayscale amplifier and high-speed digital link; no stock-monitor plug compatibility or final OEM contract assumed.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Ball documents 26-36 kHz horizontal and 40-80 Hz vertical; optional linear amplifier is 35 MHz typical. 60 Hz at the selected totals needs a qualified OEM deflection revision. Pixel clock is not analog bandwidth: test actual contrast, grayscale settling, geometry and corner focus. 56 Hz/35 kHz is a fallback engineering option, not a silently substituted retail specification.
specification.oem: Ball HD-series HD17H, 17-inch horizontal-format OEM assembly, analog/linear-video option
specification.signal_path: Logix digital pixel index -> AION palette/controller -> 4-bit intensity DAC -> level-matched Ball analog input and linear amplifier. TTL/ECL-only input is not sufficient.
specification.rgb_palette_mapping: Preserve the 12-bit RGB command format. For grayscale, equal-channel values 000,111,...,FFF map to the corresponding 16 intensity codes. Other RGB values use a documented fixed luminance mapping, with DAC/gamma calibration qualified on the actual CRT.

integration_requirements.sourcing_policy: Qualified AION 64K×1 grades for 256 KB modules: 64/128 chips for the 512 KB/1 MB shipping capacities. The 768 KB target uses paired 128 KB two-rank 16K×1 modules. Shared interface and full-population qualification pending.

memory.population_policy: Two matched 32-bit modules per capacity bank, selected independently on the 32-bit bus. Fill banks in order; all ranks require decoding and refresh. Cross-host connector/timing qualification pending.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

software_compatibility.native_40_column_mode: Native 40×25 with 8×8 cells, plus all listed 80-column modes; discover via display API.

networking.implementation: One removable NIC occupying one of the four general-purpose expansion slots; not additional integrated circuitry.
networking.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches

pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

before.name: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card
before.description: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

requirements.description: Dedicated slot; powered-off replacement only; host interface, power rails and signal integrity require qualification.
Qualification pending.

memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

display_memory.organization: Two 16K x 16-bit banks; ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Preserve independent refresh and bounded host access.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

technical_definition.athena_qualification: Existing card baseline selected; Athena host electrical/firmware compatibility remains a release gate.

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
specification.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
specification.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
specification.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
specification.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

video.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

networking.implementation: One removable NIC occupying one of the four general-purpose expansion slots; not additional integrated circuitry.
networking.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

video.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
video.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

software_compatibility.adaptive_text: Applications query usable columns/rows instead of selecting behavior from model name.
software_compatibility.native_40_column_mode: Native 40×25 with 8×8 cells, plus all listed 80-column modes; discover via display API.

networking.implementation: One removable NIC occupying one of the four general-purpose expansion slots; not additional integrated circuitry.
networking.rate_policy: Firmware-enforced host ceiling; actual common network rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

assembly_requirements.description: Remove 128 Kbit dependency

use four/eight high-density modules and two/four banks. PCB dimensions, layer stack, finish, connectors, fitted passives and reference designators

proposal.title: Date known-version editions and set their distribution quantities
proposal.reason: Preserve all 14 existing version labels, including CP/M Aurelia 1.4-derived / Platform Extensions 1.0; do not conflate the CP/M core with the extensions version. Apply first-use dates from version-pinned commercial compositions (or the explicit partner launch for external editions), with final end 1995-01-01. Apply diskette assumptions on physical media lines: Abacus 1, AION C IDE 2, full BPI suite 3, otherwise 1. BPI network clients/server are separate distributions and use 1 each; the three separately named SDK media groups use 1 each. Update paired base-part wording so each unit means one physical diskette. These are scenario defaults, not measured image sizes; retain installation and capacity qualification. Combine these edits with the edition dates to avoid overlapping proposals.

before.description: Abacus 3.0 (AIONix edition)

features: native 32-bit spreadsheet, structured-data analysis and reporting for Artemis
multiple tabs and cross-tab references; ordinary sparse worksheets coexist with schema-defined formatted-table tabs
typed columns, virtual calculated columns, unique-key lookups and read-only SQL queries
disk-backed columnar formatted-table storage with column pruning, conservative statistics-based block skipping and dataset-dependent encoding
graphical bar, line, pie and XY scatter charts in existing report layouts, with graphics preview and printing
embedded Pulse scripts through the Abacus document API
CSV and host-exported VSAM logical-record import into formatted tables
explicitly_not_assumed: background recalculation
unlimited document size or memory
guaranteed compression ratios or query throughput
full SQL database or transactional ledger engine
direct reading of arbitrary VSAM disk images
unrestricted nested-data support at the 3.0 launch

portability_contract.shared_logic: Separate application/document algorithms from platform adapters.
portability_contract.display: Query dimensions and attributes; use semantic colors and clipping.
portability_contract.memory: Bounded buffers and handles for banked objects; report allocation failures.
portability_contract.storage: Versioned, explicitly encoded records; no persisted pointers or raw C structures.
portability_contract.migration: Recompile for the target, adapt OS-specific modules and test resource limits. This does not expand the listed supported platforms.

technical_definition.programmatic_file_access: Standalone Pulse retains exclusive offline read/edit/write access to supported document versions. Embedded Pulse 3.0 uses the Abacus-owned document API; never opens a second file writer. Preserve formulas and invalidate dependent cached results.

reporting.continuity: Extend Abacus 2.0 report/document layouts, spreadsheet fields and one-off/repeating sections.
reporting.presentation: Retain standard TUI editing/navigation; add capability-aware graphical preview with titles, axes and legends. Support monochrome patterns and available display modes through the display API.
reporting.output: Print reports and charts through supported printer drivers; define pagination and refresh stale query/formula results before output.

data_interchange.bpi_continuity: Retain versioned BPI summary imports as independent planning inputs with reconciliation and decimal validation; no ledger write-back or live database connection.
data_interchange.csv: Schema-mapped CSV import with quoted fields, delimiter/character encoding selection, explicit date and decimal conventions, null handling, text preservation for identifiers and rejected-record diagnostics. Provide value-only CSV export with explicit loss-of-formulas/types warning.
data_interchange.vsam: Import host-exported sequential logical records from supported VSAM datasets using a supplied field/record layout. Host-side export (for example IDCAMS REPRO) and a documented transfer path are prerequisites; raw VSAM clusters, indexes and disk images are not desktop interchange formats.
data_interchange.vsam_conversion: Declare supported record boundaries, lengths, offsets, keys and character encoding; convert EBCDIC, supported binary, packed-decimal and zoned-decimal fields explicitly. Reject unsupported layouts without silently changing values.
data_interchange.migration: Versioned document format; preserve supported older worksheets and reports. Older Abacus/Pulse editions must reject unsupported new features before writing. Explicit value-only export is a lossy interchange option.

release_scope.launch: Flat typed formatted tables, bounded columnar processing, virtual columns, unique-key lookups, a documented read-only SQL subset, graphical reports, embedded Pulse and mapped imports.
later_milestones: Bounded nested arrays, maps and structs with explicit expansion/indexing and aggregation semantics; format extension points reserved in 3.0.
Broader query capabilities and competitive response to Lotus 1-2-3 in a later Abacus version.
release_scope.resource_policy: Qualify real Artemis 128/256 KiB configurations and later Artemis PRO separately. Record application/OS memory, storage, dataset size and timings; larger jobs may require expansion or disk-backed execution. No new minimum RAM or maximum row count is asserted.
release_scope.acceptance_workflow: Import sales records, join customer/product information, calculate margins, group by region, print a graphical report, save/reopen, then repeat using a Pulse script.
acceptance_requirements: Measure memory, disk I/O, import/query/recalculation/report times and compression on named datasets.
Verify import conversion/rejections, decimal rounding, nulls, duplicate lookup keys and join cardinality.
Verify cancellation, grouped undo, edit visibility, dependency invalidation, save recovery and unsupported-version rejection.
